facts.statement: Xinminosaurus was a cymbospondylid ichthyosaur that lived during the Middle Triassic in Guizhou Province, China.
facts.quote: Xinminosaurus is an extinct genus of cymbospondylid ichthyosaur known from the Middle Triassic (mid-late Anisian stage) of Guizhou Province, China.

facts.statement: The name Xinminosaurus combines the district of Xinmin where it was found with the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Xinmin, the district where the fossil was found, and Greek sauros, "lizard".

facts.statement: The species name means "crusher" because the animal possessed unique bulbous, laterally compressed teeth used for crushing.
facts.quote: The specific name is derived from Greek kataktes, "crusher", in reference to one of the taxon's autapomorphies - the presence of bulbous and laterally compressed crushing teeth in maxilla and posterior dentary.

facts.statement: The species is known only from a nearly complete holotype skeleton housed at the Geological Museum of Peking University.
facts.quote: Xinminosaurus is known only from the holotype GMPKU-P-1071, a nearly complete skeleton deposited in Geological Museum, Peking University.

facts.statement: The fossils were found in the upper member of the Guanling Formation within the Nicoraella kockeli biozone.
facts.quote: It was collected from the conodont Nicoraella kockeli biozone (Pelsonian of the Anisian stage), from the upper member of the Guanling Formation.

facts.statement: The holotype was discovered near Yangjuan Village in the Xinmin District of Panxian County.
facts.quote: It was found near Yangjuan Village of the Xinmin District, Panxian County.

facts.statement: Researchers have debated whether Xinminosaurus is a valid genus or merely a junior synonym of Tholodus.
facts.quote: Maisch suggested that Xinminosaurus might be a subjective junior synonym of Tholodus.

facts.statement: Maisch argued that the main difference between Tholodus and Xinminosaurus is size, with Tholodus being twice as large.
facts.quote: The only difference between the taxa, according to Maisch, is that Tholodus specimens are on average twice as large as the holotype of Xinminosaurus.

facts.statement: Mulder and Jagt (2019) suggested that the teeth of the mosasaur Globidens timorensis resemble those of the ichthyosaurs Tholodus and Xinminosaurus.
facts.quote: Mulder and Jagt (2019) demonstrated that the tooth crowns of the putative mosasaur "Globidens" timorensis from West Timor reveal a striking resemblance to those of the Triassic durophagous ichthyosaur genera Tholodus and Xinminosaurus.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton measured 2.32 meters in total length with a skull 29 centimeters long.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Xinminosaurus has a total length of 2.32 m, while its skull measures 29 centimeters long.

facts.statement: The animal's teeth were bulbous and narrow from side to side, lacking constrictions in the back of the jaws.
facts.quote: The teeth of Xinminosaurus lack constrictions. In the maxillae (back upper tooth-bearing bones) and back parts of the dentaries (lower tooth-bearing bones) they are bulbous but narrow from side to side.

facts.statement: Replacement teeth were arranged in a second row rather than being located in pulp cavities.
facts.quote: The replacement teeth of these bones were not located in the pulp cavities, instead being present as a second row of teeth.

facts.statement: The tips of the jaws may have been toothless, while the front teeth were cone-shaped.
facts.quote: The very tips of its jaws, however, may have been toothless, while the teeth at the front of the denataries are cone-shaped.

facts.statement: The skeleton possessed a total of 140 vertebrae.
facts.quote: Xinminosaurus has a total of 140 vertebrae.

facts.statement: Approximately 60 vertebrae were located in front of the hips, a high number similar to other ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: Of these, about 60 are located in front of the hips, a very high number, similar to some other ichthyosaurs.

facts.statement: The tail bent downwards at a 35-degree angle starting at the 38th caudal vertebra.
facts.quote: In Xinminosaurus, the tail is bent downwards at a 35° angle, starting at caudal vertebra 38.

facts.statement: The limb bones of Xinminosaurus were atypical for an ichthyosaur.
facts.quote: The long limb bones of Xinminosaurus are atypical for an ichthyosaur.

facts.statement: The upper arm bones featured bladelike projections on their front edges, a characteristic of ichthyopterygians.
facts.quote: The humeri (upper arm bones) of Xinminosaurus bear bladelike projections on their front edges, and Ichthyopterygian characteristic.

facts.statement: The foreflipper digits contained a small number of bones compared to other ichthyosaurs, with counts of 3, 5, 5, 5, and 2.
facts.quote: The number of bones in each digit in the foreflipper is 3, 5, 5, 5, and 2 respectively, small counts for an ichthyosaur.

facts.statement: Xinminosaurus is classified within the parent group Omphalosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Omphalosauridae

facts.statement: The family of Xinminosaurus is Omphalosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Omphalosauridae

facts.statement: Xinminosaurus belongs to the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

rejected.statement: The genus was described by Jiang et al. in 2008.
rejected.quote: Xinminosaurus is an extinct genus of cymbospondylid ichthyosaur known from the Middle Triassic (mid-late Anisian stage) of Guizhou Province, China.
